newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Inco strike bullish for nickel - Australian trade.
newsitem.headline: Inco strike bullish for nickel - Australian trade.

text.p: Australian metal dealers said they expected the strike at Inco Ltd's Sudbury operations in Canada to be bullish for the sliding nickel price.
"It should be bullish for nickel, definitely, on the day," one dealer said.
The market was illiquid in the Australian time zone so a reaction was not expected until the London Metal Exchange (LME) opened, he said.
Nickel had been under a lot of pressure, with LME stocks increasing and Russian exports typically reaching a cyclical high at this time of year, he said.
This had pushed the nickel price basis three months to its present level of about US$7,000 a tonne from $7,800 because of fund liquidation, the dealer said.
"This news should provide some support for (the price)," he said.
As earlier reported, the union representing 4,670 workers at Inco's Sudbury operations voted on Monday to reject a tentative contract agreement.
As a result, unionised workers at Sudbury will be on strike effective midnight Monday, the United Steelworkers of America said.
The strike affects unionised workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne, Ontario.

According to Inco's production plan for the current fiscal year, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper, and about four million pounds of cobalt.
